messages.author: 20cc6c6b0c022ce1
messages.subject: geom_dotplot
parts:
# Greetings,
#
# I am trying to create a graph similar to the one created below
# with the base function stripchart() using the geom_dotplot(). I am
# getting some results that are not quite what I expected...so I was
hoping
# someone might give me a little more insight on how the geom_dotplot
is
# working.
#
library(PASWR)
# Base
#
stripchart(HR ~ Team, data = Baberuth, col = c("red", "green",
"blue"),
method = "stack", pch = 19, xlab = "Home runs per season",
main = "Color dotplot of home runs \n by team")
#
# Prior to geom_dotplot()...I might have represented the base graphic
by
# jittering with lattice and ggplot2 as shown below-
#
# lattice
stripplot(Team ~ HR, data = Baberuth, jitter.data = TRUE)
#
# ggplot2
ggplot(data = Baberuth, aes(x = HR, y = Team)) +
geom_jitter(aes(x = HR, color = Team))
#
# Now trying to create something similar to the base graphic with
# the geom_dotplot...
#
# I thought the following would return similar results (ie, using
# geom_jitter() vs geom_dotplot() ) but that is not the case.
ggplot(data = Baberuth, aes(x = HR, y = Team)) + geom_jitter()
ggplot(data = Baberuth, aes(x = HR, y =Team)) + geom_dotplot()
#
# Ok, so now I am attempting to get the dots lined up with the Teams
# using facet_grid()...but this eats the Bos-N point...and it seems
that
# the call no longer works when there is only one point to be
graphed...
# is this an intended feature...if so, how might I work around this
type
# of problem to get the desired graph?
#
ggplot(data = Baberuth, aes(x = HR)) + geom_dotplot() +
facet_grid(Team ~ .)
#
# Comments suggestions most appreciated. Thanks in advance.
#
# Alan -

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: geom_dotplot
parts:
Hi - you can do it by swapping the x and y variables, and then using coord_flip:

ggplot(data = Baberuth, aes(y = HR, x =Team)) + 
  geom_dotplot(binaxis = "y", binwidth = 1) + coord_flip()


geom_dotplot behaves differently when binning along the x and y axes. When binning along x, it's sort of like using geom_histogram -- you can't specify the y position of each group because the stat that it uses, stat_bin, sets the baseline at zero and the top of the bar equal to the number of cases in each bin. 

When binning along y, it behaves sort of like geom_boxplot. You can specify the x position of each group, and the dots will use that as the baseline.

Unfortunately, I don't think it's possible to make x and y work symmetrically with the current ggplot2 code base. Hopefully at some point it will be possible to do it.

-Winston

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: geom_dotplot
parts:
Hi Alan,

There is an example of this in the excellent "Changes and Additions to
ggplot2-0.9.0", pp. 18 - 19, which boils down to

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(vs), y = mpg)) +
geom_dotplot(binaxis = "y")

For your example you just need to flip the axes:

ggplot(data = Baberuth, aes(x = Team, y = HR)) +
geom_dotplot(binaxis = "y") +
coord_flip()

and color the dots:

ggplot(data = Baberuth, aes(x = Team, y = HR, fill = Team)) +
geom_dotplot(binaxis = "y") +
coord_flip()

Best,
Ista

PS. Is the Changes and additions document posted anywhere besides the mailing
list? I'm finding it very helpful, and it would be nice to have it widely
available.
